body.statement:
Fix an intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair and define
\[
 m_n=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor,
 \qquad
 V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\},
 \qquad
 \eta_n^\star=\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_n^\star=\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-
 =\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^{n}\min\{L_r(t/n-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For every possibly randomized complete-log confidence set \(D_n=D_n(O_n,U)\), where \(U\) is independent of the experiment and identically distributed under both signs, let
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
With \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\), for every \(n\) and either sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For each \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inequality is attained within this two-sign subexperiment by a possibly randomized complete-log confidence set of maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\), for which
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+.
\]
Writing \(x=1-a_\star\), one has
\[
 \Delta_n^\star\ge d(x),\qquad
 \Delta_n^\star\longrightarrow d(x),
\]
where
\[
 d(x)=2\int_0^x\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =\begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\omega(a_\star)
 :=\exp\{-H(a_\star)\},
 \qquad
 H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du.
\]
If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\) and \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), then
\[
 H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\ge u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]
Finally, every \(q'\in\mathcal Q\) satisfies
\[
 q'(u)\ge\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\},
\]
so, for every fixed start and every \(n\), \(\bar q_\star\) maximizes the common late-void product among deterministic designs \(e_{nt}^{q'}=\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\).  All attainment assertions are confined to the displayed two-sign pair.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(g_a(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\).  The construction gives
\[
 \tau_n^\sigma=\frac{\sigma}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n),
\]
and subtraction proves the formula for \(\Delta_n^\star\).  The function \(g_{a_\star}\) is nondecreasing.  On each interval \(((t-1)/n,t/n]\),
\[
 g_{a_\star}(u)\le g_{a_\star}(t/n),
\]
so the right-Riemann sum satisfies
\[
 \Delta_n^\star
 \ge2\int_0^1g_{a_\star}(u)\,du
 =2\int_0^{1-a_\star}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =d(1-a_\star).
\]
Because \(g_{a_\star}\) is continuous, the same right-Riemann sums converge to the integral.  Splitting the integral at \(s=M/L_r\), when this point lies below \(x\), gives the two displayed branches of \(d(x)\).

Let \(V_{n,s}=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{s}\{A_{nt}=0\}\).  This event is \(\mathcal F_{n,s}\)-measurable.  Predictable randomization and the deterministic propensity imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s})
 &=\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{V_{n,s-1}}
 \Pr_\sigma(A_{ns}=0\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1})
 \right]\\
 &=\left[1-\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(s/n)/s\}\right]
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Iteration proves \(\Pr_\sigma(V_n)=\eta_n^\star\) under both signs.  Every factor is positive because the treatment propensity is at most \(\rho<1\).

For the limit, \(m_n/n\to a_\star>0\).  Thus the cap is inactive throughout \(t>m_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Put \(p_{nt}=\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\) on this range.  Since \(p_{nt}\le c/t\),
\[
 \max_{t>m_n}p_{nt}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^n p_{nt}^2
 \le c^2\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n t^{-2}longrightarrow0.
\]
For \(0\le z<1\), integration of \(z/(1-z)\) gives
\[
 0\le-\log(1-z)-z\le\frac{z^2}{2(1-z)}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \log\eta_n^\star
 =-\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n\frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}t+o(1).
\]
The function \(u\mapsto\bar q_\star(u)/u\) is continuous on the compact interval \([a_\star/2,1]\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^n\frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}t
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \frac{\bar q_\star(t/n)}{t/n}
 \longrightarrow\int_{a_\star}^1\frac{\bar q_\star(u)}u\,du
 =H(a_\star).
\]
Exponentiating proves \(\eta_n^\star\to e^{-H(a_\star)}\).

If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then \(c-L_qu\ge c/2\) throughout \([0,1]\), so \(\bar q_\star(u)=c-L_qu\) and
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1(c/u-L_q)\,du
 =c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\), the affine branch meets the floor at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\in(0,1)\).  When \(a\ge u_q\), direct integration of \((c/2)/u\) gives the first split formula.  When \(a<u_q\), splitting at \(u_q\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H(a)
 &=\int_a^{u_q}(c/u-L_q)\,du
   +\int_{u_q}^1\frac{c}{2u}\,du\\
 &=c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)
   +(c/2)\log(1/u_q),
 \end{aligned}
\]
as asserted.

We next prove the information inequality.  The assignment law is identical under both signs.  For \(t\le m_n\), one has \(t/n\le a_\star\), so both treated potential outcomes are zero.  On \(V_n\), every later unit is assigned control and also has observed outcome zero.  The propensity and regression logs are deterministic and identical.  Therefore, for every measurable set \(E\),
\[
 \Pr_+\{(O_n,U)\in E,V_n\}
 =\Pr_-\{(O_n,U)\in E,V_n\}
 =:\nu_n(E),
\]
where \(\nu_n\) is a common subprobability measure of mass \(\eta_n^\star\), dominated by both sign-specific laws.  If \(E_{\sigma,n}=\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n\}\), then
\[
 \nu_n(E_{\sigma,n}^c)
 \le\Pr_\sigma(E_{\sigma,n}^c)
 \le\gamma_n.
\]
The union bound for the finite measure \(\nu_n\) yields
\[
 \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})
 \ge\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n.
\]
On this intersection the reported set contains both causal targets, separated by \(\Delta_n^\star\).  Domination by either experimental law and nonnegativity of probabilities prove
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n^\star\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]

For attainment, take an independent \(U\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\).  On \(V_n^c\), the first treated unit after \(m_n\) has a nonzero observed outcome whose sign equals \(\sigma\); report the corresponding true singleton.  On \(V_n\), if \(\eta_n^\star>2\alpha\), allocate conditional probabilities
\[
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 1-\frac{2\alpha}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to \(\{\tau_n^+\}\), \(\{\tau_n^-\}\), and \(\{\tau_n^+,\tau_n^-\}\), respectively.  If \(\alpha<\eta_n^\star\le2\alpha\), allocate
\[
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\quad
 \frac{2\alpha-\eta_n^\star}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to the two singletons and the empty set.  If \(\eta_n^\star\le\alpha\), report the empty set on \(V_n\).  The displayed probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one in their respective cases.  Adding the certain coverage on \(V_n^c\) shows that each sign has miscoverage at most \(\alpha\).  The two-target set is the only output of positive diameter, and its unconditional probability is exactly \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\).  This proves pairwise sharpness.

Finally, take any \(q'\in\mathcal Q\).  Its anchor and Lipschitz condition imply
\[
 q'(u)\ge q'(0)-L_qu=c-L_qu,
\]
while its lower bound gives \(q'(u)\ge c/2\).  Hence \(q'(u)\ge\bar q_\star(u)\) pointwise.  Since \(z\mapsto\min\{\rho,z/t\}\) is nondecreasing and \(z\mapsto1-z\) is nonincreasing,
\[
 \prod_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\right]
 \le\eta_n^\star.
\]
Thus \(\bar q_\star\) is pointwise admissible and maximizes the finite common late-void mass for every fixed start.  When \(L_q=0\), it equals the constant profile \(c\), so the pre-existing constant-intensity theorem and its exact small-horizon diagnostic are recovered without alteration.
